points.description: States that a class definition typically contains function members (member functions/methods) and data members (variables/attributes/fields).
points.partial_credit: Award about 2.5 marks if only one of the two (data members or function members) is given, or if the answer is vague but on the right track (e.g. 'variables and access specifiers').

rubric.notes: Full marks for naming both data members (variables/attributes) and function members (functions/methods), in any wording. Part marks if only one is given or the answer is vague but related. No marks if neither is mentioned. Extra correct detail (e.g. access specifiers, constructors) is fine.
